evidence: Liv. 2.12.9: et facere et patī fortia Rōmānum est
Plin. Ep. 9.12.2: cōgitā et illum puerum esse et tē fuisse
terms.comment: Each member equal. With a negative, “neither … nor” is nec … nec.

terms.grammar: conjunction and adverb: the second member weighs more
evidence: Liv. 26.50.13: vincentem omnia cum armīs, tum benignitāte ac beneficiīs
terms.comment: “Not only … but especially”; often strengthened, cum … tum vērō (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: et facere et patī fortia Rōmānum est
phrases.english: both to do and to bear brave things is the Roman way

phrases.latin: cōgitā et illum puerum esse et tē fuisse
phrases.english: remember both that he is a boy and that you were one

phrases.latin: utrumque enim vitium est, et omnibus crēdere et nūllī
phrases.english: for both are faults, trusting everyone and trusting no one

phrases.latin: Tum pol ego et oleum et operam perdidī.
phrases.english: Then, by Pollux, I’ve wasted both my oil and my effort.

phrases.latin: vēnisse dīs simillimum juvenem, vincentem omnia cum armīs, tum benignitāte ac beneficiīs
phrases.english: that a young man most like the gods had come, conquering everything by arms and, above all, by kindness and good deeds

sources: Lewis & Short: et · Lewis & Short: cum · Lewis & Short: tum
